CNPq recently announced the results of the [Call MCTI/CNPq No. 03/2025 -
Pró-Amazônia](http://memoria2.cnpq.br/web/guest/chamadas-publicas?p_p_id=resultadosportlet_WAR_resultadoscnpqportlet_INSTANCE_0ZaM&filtro=abertas&detalha=chamadaDivulgada&idDivulgacao=12865),
and the National Institute for Amazonian Research (INPA) had three
proposals approved — among them, one that fills us with pride: the
project **"Amazonian Spectral Herbaria Network: Spectroscopy and
artificial intelligence for the automated identification of biodiversity
in Amazonian herbaria – HerbSpectra-Amazônia"**, coordinated by Dr.
Flávia Durgante, whose team and objectives are directly connected to the
spirit of SpectraPop.

This approval is a milestone for the modernization of Amazonian botanical
collections and for the advancement of spectroscopy as a complementary
tool for identifying biodiversity. And, of course, it is a great
collective achievement for all the Brazilian and international partner
institutions involved.

![Collaborative network for building spectral herbaria of the
Amazon.](../../assets/images/mapa-herbspectra-amazonia.png){fig-align="center"
width="800"}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# What is HerbSpectra-Amazônia?

The project proposes something unprecedented in Brazil: creating the
first international network of Amazonian herbaria equipped with NIR
spectroscopy technology and trained to standardize the spectral reading
of plants in scientific collections.

The central idea is simple: to digitize, in a standardized and accessible
way, the spectral signatures of Amazonian plants; to train artificial
intelligence algorithms to recognize species automatically; and to
modernize botanical taxonomy, making it faster, more reproducible and
aligned with emerging digital technologies.

For a biome with more than 15 thousand plant species, where traditional
identification demands time, specialists and ideal conditions, the
combination of AI + spectroscopy can change everything.

# An Amazonian and international collaboration network

The proposal was submitted with the support of 16 national and
international institutions, showing the reach and relevance of the
initiative. The network of executing herbaria includes:

## Five Brazilian herbaria

-   INPA – National Institute for Amazonian Research (Manaus,
    Amazonas) - coordinating hub

-   HSTM Herbarium – Federal University of Western Pará (Santarém,
    Pará)

-   MG Herbarium – Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi (Belém, Pará)

-   UFACPZ Herbarium – Federal University of Acre (Rio Branco, Acre)

-   UFRR Herbarium – Federal University of Roraima (Boa Vista, Roraima)

## Five herbaria from ACTO countries (Bolivia, Colombia, Peru and Ecuador)

All have already expressed interest in digitizing their collections, some
even starting to acquire MicroNIR spectrometers.

-   COAH Herbarium – Instituto Amazónico de Investigaciones Científicas
    SINCHI (Bogotá, Colombia)
-   HUTI Herbarium – Universidad Tecnológica Indoamérica (Quito, Ecuador)
-   LPB Herbarium – Instituto de Ecología de la Universidad Mayor de San
    Andrés/ Museo Nacional de Historia Natural (La Paz, Bolivia)
-   QCNE Herbarium – Museo Ecuatoriano de Ciencias Naturales del
    Instituto Nacional de Biodiversidad (Quito, Ecuador)
-   TKN Herbarium – Instituto de Investigación de la Universidad Nacional
    Jorge Basadre Grohmann (Tacna, Peru)

## And more:

Leading international institutions that are members of
[iHerbSpec](https://iherbspec.github.io/), such as the Harvard
University Herbaria, the Missouri Botanical Garden, Aarhus University and
the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, also take part, offering
expertise, training and global standardization.

# Why does this matter?

The Amazon is one of the most diverse regions on the planet — but also one
of the most challenging for taxonomists. Near-infrared (NIR)
spectroscopy:

-   is fast

-   is non-destructive

-   is less costly than DNA-based methods

-   and is able to recognize chemical and physical characteristics of
    plants with impressive precision.

Recent research shows that spectral signatures can corroborate molecular
results, predict functional traits and even identify species with high
accuracy.

With thousands of samples being digitized in different Amazonian herbaria,
the project will create the largest spectral database of the Amazonian
flora, something unprecedented on a global scale.

# And the AI models?

Another central axis of the project will be the development of machine
learning models — from Random Forest to neural networks and deep learning
— to recognize species, predict functional traits and test the
transferability of the models between herbaria in different countries.

The team also plans:

-   the use of XAI (SHAP, LIME) to interpret models

-   documented pipelines published on GitHub and Zenodo

-   a minimum accuracy of 85% in species identification

A true technological revolution for Amazonian botany!

# Training for the whole Amazon

The project has a strong training component, including:

-   online courses (in Portuguese and Spanish) on herbarium spectroscopy

-   in-person workshops in nine Amazonian herbaria

-   seminars on AI and biodiversity

-   a 40-hour international course on AI applied to biodiversity

-   creation of materials for science outreach and technical training

> ***In other words: the project not only does science, it also trains
> people, builds networks and modernizes entire collections.***

# A bit of what we will deliver

HerbSpectra-Amazônia foresees, among other products:

-   A consolidated international network of spectral herbaria

-   Training of more than 100 people

-   A standardized spectral database

-   AI models for species identification

-   Scientific publications and reproducible scripts

-   A closing international workshop

The schedule spans 24 months, with lasting impact for the whole Amazon
region.

# Why is this also a victory for SpectraPop?

SpectraPop, funded by FAPEAM, has been fundamental in popularizing the use
of plant spectroscopy in the Amazon, testing accessible equipment such as
the MicroNIR and bringing the technique to students, technicians and
communities.

Now, with HerbSpectra-Amazônia, this impact is multiplied: what began as
a pioneering effort in Manaus becomes a pan-Amazonian network.

# Let's celebrate together!

With pride and enthusiasm, we celebrate this achievement alongside INPA
and all the partners.

HerbSpectra-Amazônia represents the future of Amazonian botany — a future
that is faster, more integrative, more technological and more
collaborative. Soon we will share news: training sessions, workshops,
courses and the behind-the-scenes of building this mega-project.

Amazonian science remains alive, strong and innovative. And we keep
going together, illuminating biodiversity… one spectrum at a time.😅
